title: Cardiovascular Comprehensive Set 1: Microcirculation and Lymphatics (Short answer)

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism for the exchange of O_2 and CO_2 across capillary walls?
questions.modelAnswer: Simple diffusion through the endothelial cell membranes.

questions.prompt: How do water-soluble substances like glucose and amino acids typically cross the capillary endothelium?
questions.modelAnswer: Through water-filled clefts (pores) between the endothelial cells.

questions.prompt: Define the filtration coefficient (K_f) in the context of the Starling equation.
questions.modelAnswer: It represents the water permeability or hydraulic conductance of the capillary wall.

questions.prompt: Which Starling force is the primary driver of fluid filtration out of the capillary?
Explain why capillary oncotic pressure (π_c) is considered a force that opposes filtration.
questions.modelAnswer: It is the effective osmotic pressure of capillary blood due to plasma proteins, which stay in the vessel and create a force that draws water back into the capillary.

questions.prompt: Why does capillary hydrostatic pressure (P_c) typically decrease from the arteriolar end to the venous end of a capillary?
questions.modelAnswer: It falls because of the frictional resistance to flow as blood moves through the vessel.

questions.prompt: What is the typical value of interstitial hydrostatic pressure (P_i) in most tissues, and what is its role in fluid movement?
questions.modelAnswer: It is normally close to zero (or slightly negative) and acts as a force opposing filtration if positive.

questions.prompt: Describe the "reflection coefficient" (σ) and its significance for the effective osmotic pressure.
questions.modelAnswer: It is a dimensionless number (0 to 1) describing the ease with which a solute crosses a membrane; a value of 1.0 means the solute is impermeable and exerts its full osmotic effect.

questions.prompt: What happens to the net fluid movement (J_v) if the sum of the Starling forces results in a negative value?
questions.modelAnswer: Net absorption of fluid from the interstitium into the capillary will occur.

questions.prompt: How does a significant decrease in plasma protein concentration, as seen in liver failure, affect the Starling forces?
questions.modelAnswer: It decreases the capillary oncotic pressure (π_c), which reduces the force opposing filtration and increases fluid movement into the interstitium.

questions.prompt: Which type of specialized capillaries found in the liver and bone marrow are characterized by wide intercellular clefts that allow protein passage?
What is the role of the lymphatic system in maintaining interstitial fluid balance?
questions.modelAnswer: It returns excess filtered fluid and filtered proteins from the interstitium back to the vascular compartment.

questions.prompt: How do lymphatic capillaries ensure the unidirectional flow of lymph?
questions.modelAnswer: Through one-way flap valves and the use of a smooth muscle wall that contracts.

questions.prompt: Define "edema" in terms of the balance between capillary filtration and lymphatic drainage.
questions.modelAnswer: Edema occurs when the volume of interstitial fluid filtered exceeds the capacity of the lymphatics to return it to the circulation.

questions.prompt: How does arteriolar constriction reduce the likelihood of edema formation?
questions.modelAnswer: It decreases capillary hydrostatic pressure (P_c), thereby decreasing net filtration.

questions.prompt: Explain the effect of increased venous pressure on capillary hydrostatic pressure (P_c).
questions.modelAnswer: It leads to an increase in P_c, which favors filtration out of the capillary.

questions.prompt: What is the "triple response" in the skin, and which vasoactive substance is primarily responsible for the resulting "wheal"?
questions.modelAnswer: A red line, a red flare, and a wheal; the wheal is caused by histamine.

questions.prompt: By what mechanism does nitric oxide (NO) produce local relaxation of vascular smooth muscle?
questions.modelAnswer: It activates guanylate cyclase, leading to the production of cyclic GMP (cGMP).

questions.prompt: How does histamine affect the Starling forces to produce local edema at the site of tissue trauma?
questions.modelAnswer: It causes arteriolar dilation and venous constriction, which significantly increases Pc and favors filtration.
